cover.headline: India's e-bus leader with a sheet-metal business attached: the stock's own history says BUY, its cash flows do not
cover.lead: JBM Auto makes sheet-metal parts for car and truck makers (57% of FY26 revenue), tools and dies (6%) and electric buses (38%), and through its 83%-owned JV JBM Ecolife also runs buses for cities on 10-12-year gross-cost contracts. Revenue tripled in five years to ₹6,088 cr; the EBITDA margin stayed at 10-12%, debt rose to ₹3,029 cr and cash from operations was negative in FY26 as receivables and unbilled revenue piled up. Q1FY27 was solid (revenue +15%, PAT +16%) and Ecolife's ₹750 cr raise let JBM Auto cut debt by ~₹410 cr. We forecast EPS of ₹11.2 / ₹14.6 / ₹17.8 for FY27-29E. No broker note dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 could be found, so we use the house method for auto components: **P/E on Sep-28E EPS**. The stock's 51.7x forward-P/E median since Apr-2021, cut by the 8.8% auto-component de-rating, gives **47x Sep-28E EPS of ₹16.2 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY under our rule.** We flag the gap honestly: that median includes the 2023-24 e-bus re-rating (forward P/E 47-114x); without those two years the multiple would be 36.5x (≈₹590). Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹561, DCF ₹141. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: About 1,282 e-buses sold in FY26 (~24% share by its own count), a ~20,000-bus plant near Delhi, a full range from city buses to sleeper coaches, and an order pipeline of 7,000-7,500 buses to execute over 2-3 years (Crisil, Aug-2026) under PM e-Bus Sewa, PM E-DRIVE and state programmes. Outside investors (IFC, Motilal Oswal; Bain in talks per the press) are funding the operating side.

arguments.h: But the group finances its own customer
arguments.p: Much of the bus revenue is sold to JBM Ecolife, a JV that JBM Auto funded with ₹336 cr of loans, ₹302 cr of preference shares and guarantees at Mar-26. Revenue is booked as buses are built. Receivables (₹2,185 cr) and unbilled revenue (₹1,511 cr) together are ~61% of FY26 revenue; the EV segment earned 4.9% EBIT on its ₹5,129 cr of assets.

arguments.h: Earnings grow, helped by lower interest
arguments.p: We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|n1}}% in FY27E and ~13-14% after, with an EBITDA margin of {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} → {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}. EPS grows faster (+{{F.epsGrowth.0|n0}}% in FY27E) because interest falls after the Jun-2026 debt cut. Other income (₹126 cr in FY26, mostly interest, including on loans to the JV) falls to ₹{{F.otherIncome.1|num}} cr. Free cash flow stays near zero: our net debt is still ~₹2,105 cr at FY29E.

arguments.h: Valuation: cheap against its own past, expensive against its cash
arguments.p: At ₹557 JBM trades at 34.3x our Sep-28E EPS and 58.8x trailing earnings, against a 51.7x forward-P/E median since Apr-2021, and ~50% below its Feb-2024 peak. On EV/EBITDA (16x) the value is ~₹561; the DCF gives only ₹141 because working capital absorbs most of the cash. The BUY rests on the house multiple; the cross-checks are the main risk to it.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026) with the first half-year balance sheet since the debt cut: receivables, unbilled revenue and net debt.
The outcome of the EV-business fundraising (press reports of Bain Capital talks, ~US$300 mn, Aug-2026; JBM: no binding agreement) and the price it sets for the bus business.
Use of the ₹1,500 cr fundraising authority approved by the board on 30-Jul-2026 (an equity issue would dilute EPS).
Bus deliveries under PM e-Bus Sewa and PM E-DRIVE and the 500-bus DRIVN agreement; Ecolife deploying the ~2,000 buses funded by Motilal Oswal.
Crisil's expected fall in debt to ₹2,500-2,550 cr by Mar-2027 and gross current assets to ~250 days.

sections.title: Three businesses under one roof: sheet-metal parts, tools and dies, and electric buses

blocks.p: JBM Auto is the listed flagship of the JBM group, controlled by the Arya family. It reports three segments. The **Component division** (57% of FY26 revenue) presses and welds sheet-metal parts and assemblies (chassis and suspension systems, fuel and air tanks, exhaust systems, skin panels) for Indian car, utility-vehicle and truck makers; its customers include Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra and VE Commercial Vehicles. The **Tool Room** (6%) designs and builds press tools, dies and moulds for JBM and outside customers. The **OEM division**, renamed **EV Business** in Q1FY27 (38%), designs and builds electric buses (city, intercity, coaches, sleepers, airport and medical buses) and sells spares and maintenance contracts. The buses are made by JBM Electric Vehicles Pvt Ltd, 85% owned. Many of them are sold to JBM Ecolife Mobility, an 83%-owned joint venture that runs buses for cities under gross-cost contracts and is accounted for by the equity method, so its revenue and debt are not in JBM Auto's consolidated accounts.

sections.title: From a sheet-metal supplier to India's largest e-bus factory, funded partly by outside investors in the operating JV

blocks.p: For most of its life JBM Auto was a sheet-metal and tooling supplier to Indian vehicle makers; it still holds 51% of two JVs with Japan's Ogihara (automotive parts and dies), accounted for by the equity method. In 2016 it formed a JV with Solaris of Poland to make electric buses; it entered e-bus manufacturing itself in 2019 (Crisil) and won city orders under FAME II and the schemes that followed. From FY24 the bus business took off (OEM revenue ₹550 cr in FY23, ₹1,741 cr in FY24), almost entirely through government tenders on gross-cost contracts, where JBM's own JV, JBM Ecolife, is often the operator. To fund the operator, the group brought in development banks and funds at the JV level: ADB and AIIB, IFC (US$100 mn, Sep-2025) and Motilal Oswal Alternates (₹750 cr, Jun-2026).

sections.title: E-buses: a government-made market with ~46,000 buses awarded; components follow vehicle output

blocks.p: India's e-bus market is driven by government programmes: more than 90% of e-bus sales go to state transport undertakings, mostly on gross cost contracts (GCC), where a private operator buys, runs and maintains the buses and the city pays a fee per kilometre for 10-12 years. Industry e-bus sales rose from ~1,200 (FY22) to ~4,900 (FY26) (KPMG, cited in AR FY26). Programmes: PM e-Bus Sewa (10,000 buses in tier-2/3 cities; 6,862 sanctioned and 5,195 deployed by Jan-2026), PM E-DRIVE (14,028 buses for nine large cities; 13,800 allocated by Mar-2026; ₹1,500 cr in the FY27 budget), state programmes; awards of ~46,000 e-buses are due for deployment over 2-3 years (AR FY26 MD&A).

bullets: **How the market works (GCC).** The GCC model makes the operator, not the city, carry the capital: the operator funds the buses up front, recovers the cost over 10-12 years from city payments, and depends on payment-security mechanisms. JBM both makes the buses and, through its JV JBM Ecolife, runs them: the group's sales are only as good as Ecolife's funding. IFC's Sep-2025 investment came with a payment-security mechanism meant to reduce city payment risk.

**Competition.** E-bus makers include Switch Mobility (Ashok Leyland), Olectra Greentech and JBM. JBM claims ~24% of FY26 sales (1,282 buses) and ~25% in Q1FY27; VAHAN data reported in the press put it second in FY26 after Switch.

**Components.** JBM's component division sells sheet-metal assemblies, chassis and suspension parts, tanks and exhausts to Indian car, utility-vehicle and truck makers. Its growth follows Indian vehicle output and content per vehicle: segment revenue grew from ₹1,455 cr (FY20) to ₹3,443 cr (FY26), 15.4% a year, but only 8% in FY26 before picking up to 15.5% in Q1FY27 as car demand recovered after the Sep-2025 GST cut (AR FY26 MD&A).

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** in a GCC market the bus maker who can also fund and run the buses wins more tenders. That is JBM's model, and it is why its share is high. It also means the industry's capital needs (the buses, the depots, the chargers) land on operators like JBM Ecolife, and through loans and guarantees partly on JBM Auto.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the tailwind is real and JBM is one of its two biggest winners. But for JBM Auto's shareholders the benefit so far has come as revenue and receivables more than as cash: cash from operations was ₹538 cr over FY24-26, against ₹717 cr of interest paid. The bus business will create value for JBM Auto only if the operating JV funds itself and pays on time.

sections.title: Components: a steady sheet-metal supplier, growing with vehicle output at a 7-8% EBIT margin

blocks.p: The component division is JBM Auto's original business and still most of its revenue: ₹3,443 cr in FY26 (+8%), ₹894 cr in Q1FY27 (+15.5%). It earns a thin but improving margin: segment EBIT was 3-6% in FY20-22 and 7.4% / 7.9% in FY25-26, with a return of 17.0% on segment assets, the best capital return in the group after the tool room. Two customers each bought more than 10% of group revenue in FY26 (₹742 cr and ₹730 cr), most likely component customers (the note does not name them). Growth depends on Indian car, utility-vehicle and truck output and on winning parts on new models.

sections.title: E-buses: revenue up ~10x in six years at an ~11% EBIT margin, but on a balance sheet that grew even faster

blocks.p: The EV business (the OEM division until Q1FY27) had revenue of ₹2,307 cr in FY26 (+16%) and ₹460 cr in Q1FY27 (+17%), and segment EBIT of ₹251 cr (10.9%). Bus revenue is lumpy: ₹831 cr in Q4FY26 against ₹460 cr in Q1FY27, because it follows tender delivery schedules and is booked as buses are built (input method). Its segment assets rose from ₹3,765 cr to ₹5,129 cr in FY26, ₹1,364 cr more for ₹323 cr more revenue; segment liabilities (mostly suppliers) were ₹2,846 cr. EBIT on segment assets was 4.9% in FY26 (5.7% in FY25), and 11.0% on net segment assets.

blocks.h: The JV that buys the buses

blocks.p: JBM Ecolife Mobility Pvt Ltd: the GCC operating platform (buses leased to cities under gross-cost contracts in project SPVs). JBM Auto owns 83% but it is a joint venture (joint control with investors), equity-accounted; its 12 project SPVs are its subsidiaries. Investors include ADB and AIIB (US$100 mn; press reports), IFC (US$100 mn, 11-Sep-2025), Motilal Oswal Alternates (₹750 cr of CCDs and NCDs, 18-Jun-2026). At Mar-26 JBM Auto had lent ₹336 cr to JBM Ecolife (10.5%, 3 years), held ₹302 cr of 8% preference shares in it, given ₹86 cr of corporate guarantees for it and ₹224 cr for its Odisha SPV, bank guarantees for its SPVs, and pledged its Ecolife shares against Ecolife's borrowings (AR FY26 note 40/41). Ecolife Green One Mobility (100% subsidiary, a GCC SPV) is consolidated. Crisil fully consolidates Ecolife Green One and 'moderately' consolidates the other GCC SPVs because of the guarantees. Share of JV losses: ₹35.5 cr (FY25), ₹31.8 cr (FY26), ₹7.9 cr (Q1FY27). Equity-accounted carrying value of JV investments ₹59 cr (Mar-26) after losses absorbed up to the carrying amount for Ecolife.

bullets: **Why this matters for earnings.** JBM Auto books the profit on building a bus when it sells it to a GCC operator. When that operator is its own JV, the profit is real only if the JV is paid by the city and can pay JBM. Ecolife's losses come back to JBM through the equity-accounted share (₹32 cr in FY26), and its funding needs come back as loans, preference shares and guarantees.

**What changed in 2025-26.** Outside money now funds Ecolife directly: IFC (US$100 mn, Sep-2025) and Motilal Oswal Alternates (₹750 cr of convertible and plain debentures, Jun-2026, of which ₹400-420 cr was used to repay JBM Auto). Crisil says funding responsibility has been "strategically shifted" from JBM Auto to the platform and expects receivables, investments and loans from JBM Auto to fall.

**What could change next.** The press reported in Aug-2026 that Bain Capital was in talks to invest ~US$300 mn in the EV business; JBM said JBM Electric Vehicles evaluates fundraising options routinely and that nothing binding had been signed. A deal would put a price on the bus business but could also reduce JBM Auto's share of it (already 85%).

blocks.callout: **Our forecast:** EV revenue +20% / +20% / +18% in FY27-29E at 11% / 11.3% / 11.5% EBIT, taking buses to ~44% of revenue by FY29E (Crisil: above 40% within 1-2 years). The order pipeline (7,000-7,500 buses to execute over 2-3 years, Crisil) supports the volume; the constraint is funding at the operator, not demand.

sections.title: Tool room: the best margin in the group (~20% EBIT), but only 6% of revenue

blocks.p: The tool room designs and builds press tools, dies and moulds, for JBM's own presses and for outside customers. Revenue was ₹338 cr in FY26 (+11%) and ₹89 cr in Q1FY27 (+4%); EBIT ₹66 cr (19.5%), down from 27% in FY20 as the business grew. Tooling revenue is also booked over time as tools are built. Segment assets jumped to ₹587 cr in FY26 (₹464 cr in FY25), so its return on assets fell to 11.3%. We model +7% / +9% / +9% at 18% / 18.5% / 18.5% EBIT.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** No durable moat in components; a scale lead in e-buses that rests on government tenders and on the group's willingness to finance its own customer. The returns say the same: ROCE has been 12-15% for five years (Screener), roughly the cost of capital.

sections.title: Revenue tripled in five years on e-buses; the EBITDA margin stayed at 10-12% and net profit grew more slowly than debt

blocks.p: JBM Auto's consolidated revenue rose from ₹1,982 cr in FY21 to ₹6,088 cr in FY26 (Screener basis): 25% a year. Two engines drove it. The component division grew from ₹1,295 cr to ₹3,443 cr as Indian car and utility-vehicle output recovered and JBM won more content per vehicle. The OEM division (electric buses) grew from ₹459 cr to ₹2,307 cr, almost all of it after FY23, as city bus tenders under FAME II, PM e-Bus Sewa and state programmes were awarded on gross-cost contracts. The EBITDA margin did not move much: 10-12% every year since FY19, because buses earn a segment EBIT margin of ~11%, similar to the group. Net profit attributable to shareholders rose from ₹49 cr to ₹219 cr, but interest rose from ₹55 cr to ₹318 cr and other income (mostly interest charged to the group's own bus-operating JV) from ₹12 cr to ₹126 cr. FY26 EPS was ₹9.25, +8%.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** JBM Auto has grown fast, but the growth has not improved the quality of its earnings. The component business is a steady, low-margin supplier. The e-bus business has given it scale and a leading market share, but its profit comes with a large balance sheet: receivables, unbilled revenue and loans to the group's own operator. In FY26 interest absorbed 47% of EBITDA and other income was 41% of profit before tax.

bullets: **Components carried the quarter** (+15.5%), helped by stronger car and utility-vehicle output after the GST cut of Sep-2025.
**Buses grew 17% but were only ₹460 cr**, against ₹831 cr in Q4FY26: deliveries follow tender schedules and city flag-offs (Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Delhi, Panipat and others in Q1).
**Interest fell** to ₹83 cr from ₹108 cr in Q4FY26 after ~₹500 cr of long-term debt was repaid; other income stayed high at ₹31 cr. JV losses were ₹7.9 cr and the minority share ₹2.1 cr.

**Corporate news:** ~25% e-bus market share; JBM Ecolife's ₹750 cr investment from Motilal Oswal Alternates; agreement with DRIVN (an electric commercial-vehicle leasing platform) for 500 electric luxury buses; long-term debt cut by ~₹500 cr; JBM Galaxy sleeper/seater electric coach launched; fleets flagged off in Ahmedabad (155), Vadodara (130), Delhi (110), Panipat (70), Gandhinagar (40), Jamnagar (25), Ambala (20). Board approved raising up to ₹1,500 cr through securities (QIP or other routes), subject to shareholders (30-Jul-2026); a similar ₹1,500 cr enabling resolution was passed at the Sep-2025 AGM and not used.

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** JBM gives no numerical guidance and holds no calls, so the best outside view of its plans is its rating agency's. Crisil expects 14-16% revenue growth, a slightly better margin and, above all, falling debt as the JV funds itself. Our revenue and cash-accrual forecasts are close to Crisil's; we are more cautious on working capital.

sections.title: FY21-26: a ₹2,600 cr cash shortfall after interest, paid for with debt

blocks.p: JBM Auto is not a heavy capex spender (₹652 cr in FY24-26); its cash goes into working capital and into its own bus-operating JV. Over FY24-26 cash from operations was only ₹538 cr (FY26: −₹60 cr) because receivables rose by ~₹2,350 cr; investments in and loans to the JV and other investing took ₹669 cr; interest paid was ₹717 cr. The gap, ₹1,556 cr, was filled with ₹1,558 cr of net new borrowing. ROCE on Screener's basis has been 12-15% for five years and ROE 13-19%.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** the group has chosen to be both the bus maker and, through JBM Ecolife, the bus operator. That wins tenders and fills the factory, but it means JBM Auto carries part of its customer's funding. Outside money (ADB/AIIB, IFC US$100 mn in Sep-2025, Motilal Oswal ₹750 cr in Jun-2026) now funds Ecolife directly; whether it keeps doing so decides whether JBM Auto's cash flow turns positive. Our model, which keeps working capital at the pro forma FY26 ratio, has free cash flow of only ₹{{F.fcf.0|num}} / ₹{{F.fcf.1|num}} / ₹{{F.fcf.2|num}} cr in FY27-29E.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but revenue booked before delivery to a related customer, and a third of PBT from other income

bullets: **Cash conversion is poor.** Cash from operations was ₹205 cr (FY24), ₹394 cr (FY25) and ₹-60 cr (FY26) against net profit of ₹179-219 cr; free cash flow was negative in five of the last seven years (Screener).

**Revenue is recognised as buses are built.** Bus sales are recognised over time, by the share of total expected costs incurred (input method), not on delivery (AR FY26 note 47). Tooling revenue too. This is why contract assets (work done, not yet billed) reached ₹1,511 cr at Mar-26. Combined with receivables of ₹2,185 cr, unbilled revenue and receivables were ~61% of FY26 revenue.

**The customer is often a related party.** A large share of e-bus sales goes to JBM Ecolife and its SPVs, a JV that JBM Auto funds with loans, preference shares and guarantees. The related-party note in the AR is printed as rotated tables that our extraction could not read reliably; we do not quote a figure (see gaps). JBM Auto also guarantees the JV's and its SPVs' borrowings and has pledged its Ecolife shares.

**Other income is large and partly from the JV.** FY26 other income ₹138.9 cr: interest ₹92.4 cr, miscellaneous ₹35.7 cr, royalty ₹4.0 cr, rent ₹3.4 cr, subsidy ₹1.9 cr, other ₹1.5 cr (AR FY26 note 29). FY25 ₹53.6 cr. It was 41% of FY26 PBT. Our forecast cuts it to ₹98 / 88 / 88 cr as the JV loan is repaid (Q1FY27 ₹31 cr; four quarters to Jun-26 ₹121 cr).

**Segment EBIT includes items outside operations.** Segment results add up to more than group operating profit: the gap (JV losses, unallocated items and other income booked in segments) was ₹6 cr (FY24), 46 cr (FY25), 88 cr (FY26). We model it as a bridge of ₹85 / 85 / 90 cr.
**Minorities.** 15% of JBM Electric Vehicles belongs to outside holders (₹19 cr of FY26 profit). We use attributable profit throughout.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Statutory auditor Marwah & Co. LLP (unmodified opinion on FY26). No qualification and small exceptional items. But three features need watching together: revenue recognised before delivery, a large related customer funded by the group, and other income from that customer. None is improper; together they mean reported profit runs ahead of cash, as FY26 (net profit ₹219 cr, operating cash flow −₹60 cr) showed.

sections.title: Net debt ~₹2,080 cr pro forma; receivables and unbilled revenue are now two-thirds of revenue

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 JBM Auto had ₹3,029 cr of borrowings on Screener's basis (Crisil: ₹3,204 cr on its adjusted basis), against ₹130 cr of cash and ₹409 cr of investments, most of which are preference shares in and equity of its own JVs. Crisil put debt at 4.5x EBITDA and interest cover at 2.2x for FY26 (rating A/Stable, reaffirmed 5-Aug-2026). In Jun-2026 JBM Ecolife used part of Motilal Oswal's ₹750 cr to repay ₹400-420 cr to JBM Auto, which cut debt; we move ₹410 cr from working capital to net cash in our Mar-26 base (pro forma net debt ~₹2,080 cr, counting the JV investments as quasi-cash). The bigger issue is working capital: trade receivables of ₹2,185 cr (₹1,007 cr a year earlier; ₹366 cr overdue 6-12 months) and contract assets (unbilled revenue) of ₹1,511 cr, against FY26 revenue of ₹6,088 cr. Crisil expects gross current assets to fall from 297 days to ~250 days by Mar-27; our model does not assume that, so our net debt stays near ₹2,100-2,150 cr.

sections.title: Ownership: the Arya family holds 67.5%; institutions own almost none of it

blocks.p: The Arya family and its companies own 67.53% (Jun-2026), a stake unchanged for at least ten quarters. Foreign portfolio investors own 2.03%, domestic institutions 0.16% and the public 30.27% (1,82,870 shareholders). Promoters have held 67.53% in every quarter since Dec-2023; FIIs fell from 3.3% (Mar-2024) to ~2%; domestic institutions hold almost nothing (0.16%); shareholders grew from ~89,000 (Dec-2023) to ~183,000 (Jun-2026): a retail-owned stock.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** a family-controlled company with almost no institutional owners. That cuts both ways: the stock can re-rate fast when institutions arrive (an equity raise or a large EV-business deal could bring them), and it can fall fast when retail sentiment turns, as it did after Feb-2024 (−50%). The promoter stake is held through a web of group investment companies.

blocks.callout: **Where we could be wrong:** on the upside, if receivables fall as Crisil expects, interest would drop faster than our ₹310 / 300 / 300 cr and free cash flow would turn clearly positive. On the downside, bus revenue is lumpy and booked as built; a slip in city payments or in Ecolife's funding would show up first as higher receivables and interest, then as lower EPS. At our 47x, each ₹10 cr of FY28-29E net profit is worth ~₹20 a share.

sections.title: The street: no broker note we could find dated on or before 30-Sep-2026

blocks.p: Coverage is thin. No broker note dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 could be found: Trendlyne's research list for JBM Auto ends in Sep-2020 (Dolat Capital, Buy, ₹373 pre-split), the company holds no earnings calls, and press coverage of the Q1FY27 results (30-Jul-2026) and of the Bain report (21-Aug-2026) quotes no broker target. Web pages that list broker targets for JBM Auto without dates, methods or a publication date on or before our as-of date, and aggregator consensus figures that do not name brokers, are not used. With no dated broker notes, we value JBM Auto the way the market quotes it and the way the house values auto-component makers: P/E on one-year-forward EPS (Sep-28E). A sum-of-the-parts (components on P/E, e-buses on EV/EBITDA) is the natural alternative, but no note on or before 30-Sep-2026 uses it and the e-bus economics are split between JBM Auto (manufacturing, 85% owned) and the equity-accounted JV JBM Ecolife (operations), whose accounts are not disclosed; we do not build one. Olectra Greentech's P/E is shown as a sensitivity.

blocks.callout: **What the bulls say** (in press coverage, not broker notes): JBM is the e-bus leader in a market the government is building, its plant has room for 20,000 buses a year, and outside investors in its operating JV and possibly its EV business (Bain report, Aug-2026) will crystallise value. **What the bears say:** the growth is financed by the group itself, cash flow is negative and the stock already fell 50% from its 2024 peak for good reasons.

sections.title: Valuation: 47x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the cash-flow cross-checks are far lower

blocks.p: With no broker note dated on or before 30-Sep-2026, we follow how the market quotes the stock and how the house values auto-component makers: P/E on one-year-forward EPS. Our earnings year is Sep-28E (half FY28E, half FY29E), what the market will look at in September 2027. EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks only. A sum-of-the-parts would split the bus business from components, but the bus economics are shared between JBM Auto (manufacturing, 85% owned) and an equity-accounted JV whose accounts are not public, so we do not build one.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a real e-bus franchise with weak cash flow, at 34x Sep-28E EPS; BUY on the house multiple

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest or second-largest e-bus maker (~24% share, ~20,000-bus plant), a pipeline of 7,000-7,500 buses backed by national schemes, outside investors in the operating JV, and a steady sheet-metal and tooling business that grew 15.5% in Q1FY27. EPS should grow ~20-30% a year for three years as revenue grows and interest falls.

**What you are paying:** 49.5x our FY27E and 38.1x FY28E EPS for a business with an 11% EBITDA margin, ROE of 16-19% in our forecasts, free cash flow near zero and net debt of ~₹2,080 cr. That is cheap against the stock's own 51.7x forward-P/E median since Apr-2021, which is why our rule gives BUY with a target of {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). It is not cheap against cash: the DCF says ₹141 and EV/EBITDA ₹561.

**The case rests on the multiple.** 47x Sep-28E EPS (51.7x median × 0.912) is what the house rule gives; the same rule without the 2023-24 re-rating gives 36.5x (~₹590). Investors who doubt that the market will again pay ~50x for this business should treat the target as the top of a range.
**We would move to HOLD above ~₹660** and to SELL above ~₹800 on today's numbers.

**Biggest swing factor:** working capital. If receivables fall as Crisil expects, cash flow, interest and the DCF all improve; if they rise again, the P/E case weakens fast. Each 1x of multiple is ~₹16.2 a share.

statementNotes.interest@FY26: ₹318 cr (+29%): receivables doubled as JBM Auto funded the JV's fleets.
statementNotes.sales@Q4FY26: +13%: e-buses ₹831 cr in the quarter (Q3 ₹632 cr).
statementNotes.interest@Q4FY26: ₹108 cr, the peak, before the Jun-2026 repayment.
statementNotes.pat@Q1FY27: +16% (₹42 cr): interest down to ₹83 cr; JV losses ₹8 cr.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for JBM Auto, consolidated, Rs crore, Screener basis (Screener's operating profit already carries the share of losses of the equity-accounted JVs, chiefly JBM Ecolife Mobility, the e-bus operating platform). Revenue growth and EBITDA margin come from the three-segment build below (segment EBIT as the company reports it), synced by JBMA.ctx.js: EBITDA = segment EBIT - bridge + model depreciation. Net profit is attributable (JBMA.patch.js); the tax rate carries the 15% minority in JBM Electric Vehicles. The Mar-26 base is pro forma for the Rs410 cr that JBM Ecolife upstreamed in Jun-2026 to cut debt (otherTreasury: out of working capital, into net cash).
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the segment build. FY27E ~+16%: Q1FY27 +15% (components +15.5%, EV +16.7%, tool room +4%); Crisil (5-Aug-2026) expects 14-16% a year over the medium term on an order book of 7,000-7,500 e-buses to be executed over 2-3 years. FY28-29E: e-bus deliveries under PM e-Bus Sewa and the Motilal Oswal-funded 2,000-bus deployment; components grow with Indian vehicle output.
assumptions._marginWhy: From the segment build: segment EBIT margins, less the bridge, plus depreciation. FY26 11.1%, Q1FY27 10.7% (Screener basis). Crisil expects +50-60bp over the medium term as the higher-margin bus business grows and non-GCC (private) buses rise from 12% to over 25% of bus sales.
assumptions._capexWhy: Crisil (5-Aug-2026) puts capex at Rs100-150 cr a year at JBM Auto; the e-bus subsidiary also capitalises development spend (intangibles rose from Rs39 cr to Rs140 cr in FY26). FY24-26 actual: Rs228 / 122 / 302 cr (Screener). Rs220-240 cr a year.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 Rs174 cr on an average gross block of Rs2,633 cr (6.6%); FY25 6.8%. Q1FY27 Rs44 cr a quarter. 6.7% gives ~Rs185 cr in FY27E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt (Rs2,080 cr pro forma at Mar-26 after the Jun-2026 repayment), so no treasury yield; interest earned on loans to the JV and on preference shares is in otherIncome.

otherTreasury._why: Rs410 cr of loans to and receivables from JBM Ecolife that the JV repaid in Jun-2026 out of Motilal Oswal's Rs750 cr investment and that JBM Auto used to cut debt (Crisil 5-Aug-2026: Rs400-420 cr upstreamed; Q1FY27 press release: long-term debt down ~Rs500 cr). Moved from working capital to net cash in the Mar-26 base year, i.e. a pro forma balance sheet after the repayment.

assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged. FY26 Rs139 cr before a Rs13 cr exceptional charge (AR FY26 note 29): interest Rs92 cr (on loans to JBM Ecolife at 10.5%, deposits and delayed payments), miscellaneous Rs36 cr, royalty Rs4 cr, rent Rs3 cr, subsidy Rs2 cr. Q1FY27 Rs31 cr; four quarters to Jun-26 Rs121 cr as reported, Rs131 cr before the Dec-2025 exceptional charge. The Rs336 cr loan to JBM Ecolife and part of the receivables were repaid in Jun-2026 out of the Motilal Oswal money, so interest income falls: FY27E Rs98 cr (Q1 Rs31 cr, then ~Rs22 cr a quarter once ~Rs9 cr a quarter of JV-loan interest stops), FY28-29E Rs88 cr (8% preference shares in JBM Ecolife Rs302 cr = ~Rs24 cr, deposits, royalty, rent and recurring miscellaneous).
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest (bank loans, working-capital lines, bus-project loans)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs318 cr (Q4 Rs108 cr at the peak of borrowing); Q1FY27 Rs83 cr after ~Rs500 cr of long-term debt was repaid. Crisil (5-Aug-2026) expects debt to fall from Rs3,204 cr (Mar-26) to Rs2,500-2,550 cr by Mar-27. ~Rs75 cr a quarter from Q2: FY27E Rs310 cr; FY28-29E Rs300 cr because working capital keeps gross debt near Rs2,700 cr in our model (we do not assume Crisil's further fall in receivable days).
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective rate on PBT including the minority share (the engine has no minority line): FY26 tax 23.3% of PBT plus minorities 6.2% = 29.4% (PBT Rs310 cr, attributable profit Rs219 cr); Q1FY27 29.7%. Kept at 29.5%: the EV subsidiary (85% owned) grows faster, but the tax rate on Indian profits is ~25%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY24-26 payout 10-12% (Screener); Rs0.95 a share for FY26.

build._note: Segment build (Rs crore). FY26 base = AR FY26 MD&A segment table (net of inter-segment sales). Segment EBIT is profit before interest and tax as the company reports it; it includes some other income and excludes unallocated items. bridge = segment EBIT - (Screener EBITDA - depreciation): JV losses, unallocated costs and other income booked inside segments. FY24 Rs6 cr, FY25 Rs46 cr, FY26 Rs88 cr, Q1FY27 Rs22 cr.
build._why: Components: FY26 +8%, Q1FY27 +15.5% as car and UV output recovered after the Sep-2025 GST cut; +12% in FY27E (Q2-Q4 against a stronger base), then +10% / +9% with vehicle output and new parts. EBIT margin 7.4% (FY25), 7.9% (FY26), 7.8% (Q1FY27): 7.9% / 8.0% / 8.0%. Tool room: FY26 +11%, Q1 +4%; +7% / +9% / +9%; EBIT margin 20.2% (FY25), 19.5% (FY26), 16.6% (Q1): 18% / 18.5% / 18.5%. EV business: FY26 +16%, Q1 +17%; Crisil expects the bus share of revenue to rise from 36% to over 40% in 1-2 years on 7,000-7,500 buses to execute over 2-3 years, and the Motilal Oswal money funds ~2,000 more buses at JBM Ecolife: +20% / +20% / +18%. EBIT margin 10.9% (FY25 and FY26), 10.6% (Q1): 11.0% / 11.3% / 11.5% as private (non-GCC) buses rise and the plant fills (Crisil: +50-60bp for the group). Bridge (JV losses, unallocated costs, other income booked in segments) Rs88 cr in FY26, Rs22 cr in Q1FY27: Rs85 / 85 / 90 cr.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical vehicle volumes, tender-driven bus orders, a JV customer funded by the group and net debt of ~Rs2,100 cr (~14% of enterprise value at the 30-Sep close). The engine discounts at the cost of equity; we set beta 1.05 (Ke 12.8%) so that the rate equals our WACC: Ke ~13.7% (beta 1.2) and an after-tax cost of debt of ~6.5% weighted 86/14 give ~12.7%.
dcf._tgWhy: House range 5-6%: 6% (bus electrification and vehicle output keep nominal growth above GDP for long).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~13% to 9% over ten years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin 11.5% in steady state (FY19-26 range 10-12%; buses lift it slightly).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 3% of revenue (FY24-26: 2-5%); depreciation 2.6% (FY26 2.9%). Working capital stays at 30% of revenue (the engine holds it at the pro forma FY26 ratio), which is what makes free cash flow thin.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: E-bus deliveries beat the 7,000-7,500-bus execution plan, private and export bus sales lift the EV margin towards 13%, receivables fall as Ecolife funds itself, and car output keeps components growing in double digits: growth ~4pp a year higher and EBITDA margin +0.7pp.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: City payments slow, Ecolife cannot raise enough money and JBM Auto has to fund its JV again (as in FY26), bus tenders are won at thinner prices and a vehicle downturn hits components: growth ~5pp a year lower and EBITDA margin -1.2pp.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the market quotes JBM Auto and how the house values auto-component makers: P/E on Sep-28E EPS (no broker note dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 was found). Multiple derived in tools/authoring/JBMA.ctx.js: own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 (no trough years) times the auto-component sector de-rating at 30-Sep-2026 (PLAYBOOK 4, 7c), nearest half-turn; written by syncMultiples().

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Separates the operating business from net debt. Multiple derived in JBMA.ctx.js from the stock's own trailing EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 and the same sector move, restated from trailing to Sep-28E EBITDA; net debt (incl. JV preference shares at book) deducted.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 10-year FCFF at 12.8% (Ke set equal to our WACC) and 6% terminal growth, less net debt. Working capital stays at the pro forma FY26 30% of revenue; no deduction for the 15% minority in the EV subsidiary.
